title: Biblical Hebrew: from the alphabet to Genesis 1
text: Leningrad codex as built in orig/ot (STEPBible TAHOT), split into its morphemes
note: Hand-written lesson plan. vocab lists Strong's numbers from vocab.json: words (the 250), the passage supplement, and morphemes (prefixes and suffixes, H9xxx), each taught once, in frequency order within a lesson. exampleRefs are references only: verse text is read from orig/ot at display time. No Hebrew is typed here except in notes; paradigm tables live in paradigms.json, the alphabet in alphabet.json. alphabetSections (alphabet lessons) = which parts of alphabet.json the lesson shows: consonants [from, to] by order and named parts. recognition = grammar a lesson covers by a note rather than a table (used by the grammar coverage check).

lessons.title: The consonants, part 1: alef to kaf
goals: Recognize the first eleven letters of the Hebrew alphabet and their names.
Say each one with its sound, using the English sound-alikes.
See that Hebrew is read from right to left.

lessons.title: The consonants, part 2: lamed to tav
goals: Recognize the last eleven letters, including shin and sin.
Recognize the five final forms used at the end of a word.
Find every letter in a short verse.

lessons.title: The dot in the letter: begadkephat, dagesh and mappiq
goals: Learn the six begadkephat letters and how a dot changes b/v, k/kh and p/f.
Tell the dagesh lene (hard sound) from the dagesh forte (a doubled letter).
Recognize mappiq in a final he.

lessons.title: The vowels
goals: Learn the vowel signs and their sounds: a, e, i, o, u.
Know which vowels are counted long and which short, and the vowel letters vav and yod.
Read the furtive patach in the word for spirit (ruach).

lessons.title: Shewa, syllables and reading aloud
goals: Tell a vocal shewa from a silent one, and read the three hateph vowels.
Divide a word into syllables and find the stressed one.
Recognize maqqef and sof pasuq, leave the cantillation marks aside for now, and read Genesis 1:1 aloud.

lessons.title: First words: God, heaven, earth, day
goals: Learn fourteen common nouns, most of them in Genesis 1.
Read the divine names Elohim and YHWH (read aloud as Adonai, "the LORD").
Find these words in Genesis 1.

lessons.title: The article: the
goals: See that "the" is a prefix, ha, joined to its noun, and that Hebrew has no word for "a".
Learn its three forms and why the letter after it is doubled.
Read "the heavens" and "the earth" in Genesis 1:1.

lessons.title: And, in, to, like, from: the little prefixes
goals: Learn the conjunction ve ("and") and its other spellings.
Learn the prepositions joined to the next word (be, le, ke) and mi(n), and how they merge with the article.
Learn the common prepositions written as words: on, to, until, with, between.
lessons.grammarTopic: The conjunction vav; inseparable prepositions; preposition + article

lessons.title: Nouns: masculine and feminine, singular and plural
goals: See that every noun is masculine or feminine.
Learn the plural endings: -im (masculine) and -ot (feminine).
Learn fourteen more nouns.

lessons.title: The construct state: the word of the LORD
goals: Understand the construct chain: a noun joined to the next one with "of".
Recognize the shortened construct forms, singular and plural.
Read "the face of the deep" and "the Spirit of God" in Genesis 1:2.

lessons.title: Adjectives: great and good
goals: See that an adjective agrees with its noun in gender and number.
Tell an adjective that describes ("a good land") from one that states ("the land is good").
Learn ten common adjectives.

lessons.title: Numbers: one to a thousand
goals: Learn the numbers one to ten, twenty, a hundred and a thousand.
See that "one" has a masculine and a feminine form.
Read "day one" at the end of Genesis 1:5.

lessons.title: The object marker and small words: et, asher, ki, lo
goals: Learn et, which marks the definite direct object and is not translated.
Learn the small words for which, for/that, not, if, also, behold.
Find et twice in Genesis 1:1 and ki in Genesis 1:4.
lessons.grammarTopic: The object marker; relative, conjunctions and negatives

lessons.title: Pronouns: I, you, he, this
goals: Learn the independent personal pronouns.
Learn this, these, who? and what?, and the he that asks a question.
See why Hebrew uses a pronoun when the verb already shows the subject.

lessons.title: People and the body
goals: Learn twelve nouns for people and the body.
Notice the ones that are feminine without an -ah ending.
Read short verses with the words learned so far.

lessons.title: Possessive suffixes: my, your, his (recognition)
goals: See that "my", "your", "his" are endings joined to the noun.
Recognize the ten possessive suffixes on the word for God.
Read "our God" and "your God" in a verse.

lessons.title: Object suffixes: me, you, him (recognition)
goals: Recognize the pronoun suffixes on prepositions ("to me", "to him").
Recognize them on the object marker ("him", "them").
See that the same endings are joined to verbs.
lessons.grammarTopic: Pronominal suffixes on prepositions and the object marker (recognition)

lessons.title: Land and living things
goals: Learn thirteen nouns for land, animals and food.
Notice the words that turn up in the creation account (sea, field, ground, animal).
Read short verses with the words learned so far.

lessons.title: The verb: the Qal perfect
goals: Learn what a root is: three letters that carry the meaning.
Learn the Qal perfect of a strong verb, shamar ("to keep"): completed action, endings after the root.
Read the perfects in Genesis 1:1 (bara, "he created") and 1:2.

lessons.title: The Qal imperfect and the jussive
goals: Learn the Qal imperfect: prefixes before the root, for action not yet complete.
Recognize the jussive, a short imperfect meaning "let …".
Read "let there be light" in Genesis 1:3.

lessons.title: And God said: the wayyiqtol
goals: Learn the vav consecutive with the imperfect, the tense that tells a story in the past.
Recognize it by va- and the doubled letter after it.
Read the chain of wayyiqtols in Genesis 1:3–5.

lessons.title: The verb "to be": hayah
goals: Learn the forms of hayah that Genesis 1 uses: was, let there be, and there was.
See that a sentence often has no verb for "is".
Learn words of time and existence: there is not, now, forever.

lessons.title: Names: Israel, David, Moses
goals: Learn the eighteen names among the most frequent words.
Read the divine names with their pointing.
Notice the names that end in -ah or -el.

lessons.title: Other stems: Piel and Hiphil (recognition)
goals: See that a root can be used in different stems that change its meaning (simple, intensive, causative).
Recognize the Piel by its doubled middle letter and the Hiphil by its a-vowel prefix.
Read "hovering" (Piel, 1:2) and "and he separated" (Hiphil, 1:4).

lessons.title: Participles and weak verbs (recognition)
goals: Learn the participle: a verb used like an adjective ("dwelling, one who dwells").
Recognize verbs whose roots have a weak letter, such as those with a middle vav (mut, qum).
Learn thirteen more verbs.

lessons.title: Small endings (recognition)
goals: Recognize the he of direction ("toward"), as in "toward the land".
Recognize the pronoun endings that act as a subject on an infinitive or on hinneh ("here I am").
Know the extra he and nun endings that do not change the meaning.
lessons.grammarTopic: Directional he; subject suffixes; paragogic endings (recognition)

lessons.title: Worship and covenant
goals: Learn sixteen words of worship, sin and covenant.
Notice the ones that come in Leviticus and the Psalms.
Read short verses with the words learned so far.

lessons.title: Camp, war and everyday things
goals: Learn twelve more common nouns.
Read short verses with the words learned so far.

lessons.title: Words for Genesis 1
goals: Learn the two words outside the 250 that come more than once in Genesis 1:1–5: light and darkness.
See each one in the verses where it appears.
Leave the one-time words of the passage to the help shown in the reading lesson.

lessons.title: Reading Genesis 1:1–5
goals: Read Genesis 1:1–5 in Hebrew, word by word, with help for the words and parts not yet learned.
Take each word apart into its prefixes, word and suffix.
Follow the story from "in the beginning" to "day one".
